newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Central African truce to be extended - government.
newsitem.headline: Central African truce to be extended - government.

text.p: Army mutineers and loyalists troops have agreed to extend a ceasefire in fighting in the Central African Republic capital Bangui, a presidential spokesman said on Sunday.
"The two sides will sign this afternoon for the extension of the truce," spokesman Theophile Doumba told Reuters. He said the length of the extension had not been decided.
The breakthrough was announced as thousands of Bangui residents fled to the countryside ahead of Sunday's expiry of a 15-day ceasefire brokered by four African presidents.

The latest agreement follows more than a week of difficult mediation by former Malian military ruler General Amadou Toumani Toure, who had been joined later by the French ambassador, sources close to the talks said.

French troops based in the former colony under bilateral accords helped keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power during a violent mutiny last May and have been backing loyalist forces in the latest revolt. Mutineers hardened pay grievances into a campaign for Patasse to step down.
